summary: Intermittent upstream process crashes and elevated 5xx during short-lived microbursts (keepalive fd leak hypothesis)
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC NovaSearch observed a pattern of intermittent 5xx errors returned to a small percentage (~3-5%) of requests during high-frequency short-lived request bursts from their dedicated pool. Impact: customer latency spikes and ~3% error rate increase over 15 minute windows; most affected endpoints are short chat completions and single-turn embed calls. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod/us-east-1 using rw-infer-base-v2 pinned model. Symptoms: - API gateway returns 502/503 to client. - Upstream runtime processes (ephemeral worker) show sudden exits (SIGABRT or OOM-like) in kmsg. - Accept queue grows briefly, then recovers as autoscaler spawns extra ephemerals. - Errors correlate with tight bursts of small payloads from customer side (many connections <200ms).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a client to fire 200 concurrent short-lived requests (payloads <1KB) over 30s with connection per-request (no keepalive reuse).
2) Observe apigw accept queue and ephemeral worker churn in us-east-1 serving pool for the customer's tenant.
3) Repeat at 3x baseline concurrency to trigger ephemeral spawn/shutdown cycles.
4) Watch for intermittent 502/503 responses within the burst window and check runtime logs for worker exits.

comments: 2026-03-10T10:00Z - Support (Aisha): Received initial report from NovaSearch CS about ~3-5% 5xx increase during morning ingest. Customer attached request traces and sample timestamps.
2026-03-10T10:30Z - SRE (Marcus): Initial triage shows short-lived bursts correlate with accept-queue growth and ephemeral worker churn. Marking as high priority and adding on-call infra.

2026-03-10T11:10Z - SRE (Marcus): Found repeated SIGABRTs in ephemeral logs; kernel OOMs also recorded shortly after. Hypothesis: frequent connect/close pattern causing keepalive/proxy fd accumulation and causing downstream resource pressure on runtime leading to crashes.

2026-03-10T12:45Z - Dev (Lina Cho): Added pprof snapshot for runtime; saw thread stacks stuck in accept() cleanup path and delayed socket close handling. Possible leak window ~1.5-2s under heavy connect churn.

2026-03-11T08:00Z - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed they can temporarily batch requests or reuse keepalive; doing that reduces observed error rate to baseline. NovaSearch requests a fix or a mitigation that doesn't require changes to their client.

2026-03-12T09:20Z - SRE (Marcus): Deployed temporary proxy knob: extend keepalive idle timeout and increased kernel fd reclaim frequency on dedicated nodes for NovaSearch pool. Error rate dropped to <0.5% during replicated tests. Preparing patch for proxy close-path handling.
2026-03-12T12:00Z - Dev (Lina): Created GitHub PR #4389 to address socket close race in proxy; added unit + integration tests reproducing microburst pattern.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Keepalive handling race in edge proxy leads to fd accounting leak for short-lived connections; proxied sockets linger, filling per-process fd tables until runtime eviction/kill paths are exercised.
Hypothesis 2: Frequent ephemeral spawn/teardown causes transient NVML/resource fragmentation on GPUs leading to OOM-like symptoms when combined with high accept queue pressure.
Observed: fd_count on proxy processes increased by ~14 FDs over 45s during microbursts. After temporary keepalive knob, fd_count stayed stable under same synthetic load.

Observed: Runtime crash stacks indicate aborts in allocator code paths shortly after a spike in accepted connections. No explicit libc trace indicating double-free, but memory pressure rose rapidly when many ephemerals overlapped.
Mitigation validated: Increasing keepalive reuse on proxy (reuse connections) reduced incidence; client-side keepalive had same effect but customer prefers server-side fix.
Next steps: backport proxy close-path fix; add runtime defensive guard to limit concurrent ephemeral ramp; tune autoscaler cooldown to avoid tight spawn/shutdown loops.
Related artifacts: apigw dashboard (grafana/dashboard/AGW-conn-accept), runtime crash traces (s3://redwood-logs/nova/2026-03-10/)
Linked incidents: SUP-472901 (conn thrashing causing upstream crashloop) - similar surface but different root cause suspected (keeps vs. kvcache).
resolution: Mitigation applied 2026-03-12: extended proxy keepalive reuse and adjusted node kernel timers on dedicated-nova pool which reduced fd accumulation and eliminated 5xx spikes in replicated load tests. Created PR #4389 to fix proxy socket close race; PR passed CI and scheduled for canary on 2026-03-15. Follow-ups: patch runtime to hard-limit ephemeral ramp and update autoscaler cooldown thresholds for dedicated pools (task assigned to infra team). Customer notified and agreed to monitor; will re-open if regressions observed.
